title: Cohomological dimension of the base field
statement:
If $K$ is an algebraically closed field, then $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)=0$. If
$K$ is a finite field, then $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)\leq1$.

proof.text: For algebraically closed K, use [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] and [det-cd-etale-comparison] at c=0, with the identity of the affine spectrum as auxiliary qcqs morphism. The result takes values in WithTop ℕ; zero_le and the upper bound imply equality. No separate nonzero degree-zero sheaf is needed.

For finite K, [det-base-field-cd-galois-group] gives Frobenius τ and an isomorphism e from Gal(Ksep/K) to the profinite completion of ℤ, with e(τ)=η(1). The image of ℤ is dense in its completion, hence the powers of τ are dense. For each N>0, extend integer reduction modulo N through the completion universal property and compose with e. This gives a continuous cyclic quotient taking τ to one.

For a torsion étale sheaf F, its geometric fibre M is torsion: the fibre preserves filtered colimits and addition, so every germ is locally represented by a torsion section. Apply [lem-base-field-profinite-cyclic-torsion-cohomology] using the generator and quotients from the previous step. It gives vanishing of discrete Galois H^q for q≥2, via finite cyclic partial sums at level ae, norm cancellation and coinduced dimension shifting.

Use [lem-base-field-etale-galois-cohomology] to identify sheaf H with this discrete Galois cohomology. The existing source nonempty_sheafH_extDerivedIso identifies sheaf H with the Ext-derived étale cohomology in HasTorsionEtaleCohomologicalDimensionLE. Therefore every torsion étale sheaf vanishes above degree one. Apply [det-cd-etale-comparison] at c=1, with the identity of the affine spectrum as auxiliary qcqs morphism.
